;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[United Nations]] [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|Secretary-General]] [[António Guterres]] warns [[Israel]] to use "extreme caution" as further protests are held at the [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]n border. [[Israeli Defence Forces]] open fire again, killing at least seven [[Palestinians]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/06/israel-warned-un-protesters-head-for-gaza-demonstrations (''The Guardian'')]
**Protestors begin burning tyres at the border. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/07/hundreds-funeral-palestinian-journalist-gaza (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Moro conflict]]
**Acting on a tipoff about a planned attack, authorities in [[Shariff Aguak]] detain two suspected would-be bombers and disable an [[improvised explosive device]]. [https://www.philstar.com/nation/2018/04/07/1803748/vigilant-residents-foil-bomb-attack-maguindanao (''Philstar Global'')]
*[[Terrorism in the Netherlands]]
**The [[Netherlands|Dutch]] Court of Appeal increases the sentence of a man who twice attempted to travel to [[Syria]] from 31 months partially suspended to 40 months. The man was previously convicted of preparing [[terrorism|terrorist]] crimes and trying to participate in a terrorist organisation. [http://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2018/04/dutch-terror-suspects-gets-higher-sentence-on-appeal/ (Dutch News)]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Metropolitan Police|Police]] announce they will expand [[Project Servator]] to cover [[London]]. Project Servator involves the deployment of hundreds of armed counterterror officers in a bid to rapidly swarm potential terrorists. [https://news.sky.com/story/hundreds-of-specially-trained-police-ready-to-swarm-terror-targets-in-london-11318002 (Sky News)]

;Arts and cultures
*[[Weinstein effect]]
**Three members of the [[Swedish Academy]] leave their seats after failing to oust another member whose husband is accused of sexual misconduct including raping young female writers. [https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/three-members-leave-the-swedish-academy/ (''Expressen'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**A report reveals that 2017 saw over ten thousand new businesses in the technology sector throughout the [[United Kingdom]], with all areas seeing growth over 2016. [[Scotland]] saw a 77% increase with 440 new firms. [https://www.scotsman.com/future-scotland/tech/tech-company-start-ups-in-scotland-jump-by-77-per-cent-1-4720016 (''The Scotsman'')]
*[[First Trump tariffs|Trump tariffs]]
**U.S. stocks drop by about 2 percent in light of U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariff statement yesterday concerning Chinese imports. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-stocks/wall-street-ends-down-2-percent-as-u-s-china-trade-fears-intensify-idUSKCN1HD1JV (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Humboldt Broncos bus crash]] 
**A transport and a bus carrying the [[Humboldt Broncos]] [[junior ice hockey]] team collide north of [[Tisdale, Saskatchewan|Tisdale]], [[Saskatchewan]], [[Canada]], en route to a play-off game against the [[Nipawin Hawks]], killing 15 people. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/multiple-fatalities-in-bus-crash-involving-saskatchewan-junior-hockey-team-1.3875235 (CTV News)] [http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/nipawin-humboldt-bus-crash-1.4609554 (CBC)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-43679808 (BBC)]
*A bus crashes near [[Genting Highlands]] in [[Bentong]], [[Pahang]], [[Malaysia]], hitting a car and a barrier. Twenty-three people are injured, including sixteen [[China|Chinese]] tourists. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/genting-highlands-bus-accident-tourists-injured-10113920 (Channel NewsAsia)]
*A helicopter crash in [[Istanbul]] kills five and injures seven. [http://tass.com/politics/934821 (T.A.A.S.)]

;Health and environment
*[[Newfoundland and Labrador]], [[Canada]], invites bids for oil and gas exploration at Northeast Newfoundland Slope, a protected marine area that was closed to fishing in December. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/newfoundland-labrador/cnlopb-oil-exploration-wwf-ffaw-1.4608502 (CBC)]

;International relations 
*[[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act]]
**The [[United States]] imposes sanctions on twelve [[Russia]]n owned companies, a Russian arms exporter, and a bank. The U.S. cites multiple reasons, including [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|Russian meddling in the 2016 elections]] and military engagements in [[Ukraine]], [[Crimea]], and [[Syria]], among others. [http://abcnews.go.com/Politics/trump-admin-hits-putins-circle-sanctions-russian-oligarchs/story?id=54294201 (ABC News)]
*[[Australia]] says it will prevent the departure of a ship due to carry 65,000 sheep to the [[Middle East]] next week unless the operators can reassure the government of the [[animal welfare|animals' welfare]]. The government launched an investigation yesterday after a video depicting conditions on the ship emerged. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/06/live-export-ship-banned-from-leaving-dock-unless-welfare-conditions-met (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Impeachment of Park Geun-hye]]
**Former [[President of South Korea|President]] of [[South Korea]] [[Park Geun-hye]] is sentenced to 24 years in prison and an ￦18 billion fine for bribery, coercion, and abuse of power, among other charges. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/06/world/asia/park-geun-hye-south-korea.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**[[Salisbury District Hospital]] says poisoned spy [[Sergei Skripal]] is no longer critically ill, responding well to treatment, and "improving rapidly". His daughter was previously revealed to have regained consciousness. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-43671958 (BBC)]
**Viktoria Skripal, a cousin of Yulia, states the poisoned pair suffered [[food poisoning]] rather than an attack with a [[nerve agent]]. Hours later she is denied a visa to visit her relatives in hospital. [https://news.sky.com/story/salisbury-attack-yulia-and-sergei-skripals-relative-refused-entry-to-britain-11319366 (Sky)]
*[[List of killings by law enforcement officers in the United States, April 2018|Killings by law enforcement officers in the United States in April 2018]]
**Hundreds protest the Wednesday fatal shooting of Saheed Vassell by [[New York Police Department|police]] in [[Brooklyn, New York|Brooklyn]], [[New York State|New York]], after a pipe he was holding was mistaken for a gun. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43663448 (BBC)]
*[[FOSTA-SESTA|Stop Enabling Sex Traffickers Act]]
**Several U.S. federal authorities led by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] seize the personal ad website [[Backpage]] in an effort to stop alleged [[Human trafficking in the United States|human trafficking]], including that of minors. Its co-founders Michael Lacey and James Larkin were also charged with 93 counts of human trafficking. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-backpage-justice/sex-ads-website-backpage-com-seized-by-u-s-authorities-posting-idUSKCN1HD2QP (Reuters)] [https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-investigations/2018/04/06/backpage-executive-michael-lacey-indicted-prostitution-charges/310430001/ (''Arizona Central'')]
*[[Sexual offences in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Glasgow]] [[Sheriff Court]] sentences [[HMP Barlinnie]] [[prison officer]] Brian Johnstone to three years imprisonment for repeatedly sexually assaulting two inmates in the showers and their cells between 2013 and 2016. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-43670870 (BBC)]
*[[ValuJet Flight 592]]
**The [[FBI]] offers a [[US$]]10,000 reward for information leading to the capture of mechanic Mauro Ociel Valenzuela-Reyes, who is accused of triggering the 1996 disaster by mispackaging oxygen cylinders that caught fire in the [[DC-9]]'s hold. He fled justice in 1999. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/06/us/valujet-fugitive-reward/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**A [[Central Criminal Court (England and Wales)|Central Criminal Court]] judge sentences [[Holland|Dutch]]-[[Somalia|Somali]] terror convict Aweys Shikhey to eight years with an [[Sentencing in England and Wales#Extended sentences|extended licence]] of four years. Shikhey received international attention for fantasy chats with a [[Kenya]]n online about murdering [[David Cameron]], Queen [[Elizabeth II]], [[Judaism|Jews]], and [[association football|football]] fans. [http://jewishnews.timesofisrael.com/somalian-who-planned-attack-on-jews-jailed-for-trying-to-join-isis/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://nltimes.nl/2018/04/06/british-court-sentences-dutch-man-8-years-terrorism (NLTimes.nl)]
*[[2018 in UFC]]
**[[Ireland|Irish]] [[mixed martial arts]] fighter [[Conor McGregor]] appears in court and is released on bail after being charged with [[UFC 223#Conor McGregor and team assault on bus|assault and criminal mischief]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/43665867 (BBC)]
*[[Human rights in North Korea]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] rejects a petition to investigate [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong Un]] for [[war crimes]]. The petition by [[Japan]]ese families of alleged victims was turned down because the alleged wrongdoing predates Japan's 2007 joining of the ICC. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20180407_07/ (NHK)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**[[Carles Puigdemont]] is released on bail, following the German judge's decision that he cannot be extradited for rebellion. However, proceedings for misuse of public funds are being considered against Puigdemont. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/05/german-court-says-carles-puigdemont-can-be-released-on-bail (''The Guardian'')]
**Puigdemont calls for the opening of dialogue with [[Spain]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43669396 (BBC)]
*[[2017–18 United States political sexual scandals]]
**U.S. Representative [[Blake Farenthold]] announces his resignation from Congress. [https://www.npr.org/2018/04/06/600343808/under-fire-for-alleged-sexual-harassment-texas-rep-blake-farenthold-resigns (NPR)]

;Science and technology
*[[Facebook and Cambridge Analytica data breach]]
**[[Facebook]] states that people running popular pages will now have to verify their identity as part of its continued efforts to stem [[fake news]] and [[propaganda]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-43676733 (BBC)]
**Facebook suspends [[AggregateIQ]], a [[Canada|Canadian]] data firm, over concerns about possible data misuse. AggregateIQ was used by the Vote Leave campaign during the [[United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, 2016|2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-43680969 (BBC)]
*[[SpaceShipTwo]]
**[[Virgin Galactic]] successfully tests [[VSS Unity]], the first test since an [[VSS Enterprise crash|October 2014 crash]] destroyed a previous version, [[VSS Enterprise]]. [http://www.euronews.com/2018/04/06/virgin-galactic-tests-rocket-ship-three-years-after-fatal-accident-the-aircraft-landed-saf (Euronews)]
